label: Deadline guide · 9 months and 1 day, 12 months
title: Corporation tax: pay 9 months and 1 day after your year end, file the CT600 within 12 months
summary: The tax is due before the return. The two corporation tax deadlines, the late filing penalties, and what happens after 6 months.
body:
Corporation tax has two separate deadlines, and the payment comes first.

The deadlines

  • Pay the corporation tax, or tell HMRC the company owes none: 9 months and 1 day after the accounting period ends. A year ending 31 March means paying by 1 January.
  • File the Company Tax Return (CT600): 12 months after the accounting period ends.

You must file a return even if the company made a loss or has no tax to pay. An accounting period for corporation tax cannot be longer than 12 months, so a company's first accounts can need two returns and two payment dates.

Late filing penalties

  • 1 day late: £200
  • 3 months late: another £200
  • 6 months late: HMRC estimates the tax and adds 10% of the unpaid tax
  • 12 months late: another 10% of any unpaid tax

If the return is late three times in a row, the £200 penalties become £1,000 each. After 6 months HMRC issues a 'tax determination' of the tax it thinks you owe, which cannot be appealed: you have to pay and file the return.

What I would do

  • Prepare the accounts and CT600 together, early, so you know the tax figure before the 9-month payment date.
  • Put money aside for corporation tax every month rather than at the year end.
